THIS MFA IS FILED U/S.173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DT.05.02.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.1460/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE XIX ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSE JUDGE, MACT, XLI ACMM, BENGALURU, (SCCH-17),
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 05.02.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-17) in MVC.No.1460/2016.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequate and meagre compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the appellants seek an enhancement of compensation.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both parties.
3. The appellants filed this appeal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Lakhs only) for the death of Muniyappa.

sentences.text: The appellants filed a claim petition claiming compensation for the death of Muniyappa, who died in the accident that occurred on 13.12.2015.
It is alleged that on 13.12.2015 at about 9.00 pm, the deceased was walking on the left side of Devanahalli-Hosakote NH-207 road, in front of the house of Muniraju at Kammasandra village.
At that time, a TATA 407 Tempo came in a rash and negligent manner, came to the wrong side of the road, and dashed to the deceased Muniyappa.
He has sustained injuries and shifted to various hospitals, where he succumbed to the injuries on 15.12.2015.
He was hale and healthy prior to the accident, was earning Rs.15,000/- pm by working as a Mason, and this accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Tempo.

Hence, they claimed the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-.
6.
In response to the notice, the respondent/owner of the vehicle placed an ex-parte.

The Insurance Company filed a statement of objections, denying the rash and negligent driving, and contended that the accident occurred on the National Highway, where the deceased should have been careful while walking on the road and while crossing the road, which he has not done, during the night hours on the National Highway.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the liability of the deceased at 10%.
Accordingly, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1.

Whether petitioners prove that on 13.12.15 at about 9.00 p.m., when the deceased was proceeding on foot in front of Muniraju house at Kammasandra Village,
Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru District, met with an accident, sustained injuries and succumbs to the same due to actionable negligence on the part of driver of TATA 407 vehicle bearing No.KA-24-A-1196 as alleged?
2. Whether petitioners prove the age, occupation and income of deceased?
3. Whether R2 proves that there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy?
4. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
5. What order or award?
8.
To prove the case of the claimants, the first petitioner was examined as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents, but the respondents did not adduce any evidence.

Accordingly, the Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs. 9,88,366/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per Smt. Kanthamma vs Sri K L Manjunath on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164656946/
3 annum and allowed the NC: 2024:KHC:27351 petition in part.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the same the claimants are before this court.
9. Learned counsel for the appellants has contended that the Tribunal committed an error in fastening the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased at 10%, which is not correct.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver.

A Charge sheet was filed against the driver,
but no evidence was adduced by the respondents.

Such being the case, fixing the liability on the deceased is not correct, and it is further contended that the Tribunal committed an error in deducting 50% of the amount towards the personal expenditure.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has supported the judgment of the Tribunal and contended that the accident occurred on the National Highway, where the deceased should have been careful while walking on the road and while crossing the road, which he has not NC:
2024:KHC:27351 done, during the night hours on the National Highway.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly fixed the liability of the deceased at 10%, which need not be interfered with.

Hence,
prayed for the dismissal of the appeal.

11. Having heard the arguments and perused the records, the points that arise for my consideration are as follows:
1.
Whether the tribunal is justified in fastening the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased at 10%?
2. Whether the appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?

12. On the other hand, the FIR - Ex.P1, complaint - Ex.P2, additional complaint - Ex.P4, Charge sheet - Ex.P5, spot mahazar - Ex.P6 and other police documents reveal that this accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo.

Though respondent No.2 has made the contention that there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, they NC:
2024:KHC:27351 have not led any evidence to prove their contentions except cross-examination.
The driver of the tempo was not before the court and had no evidence to show.
There is no contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
On the other hand, the police records and evidence of the appellants clearly depict that this accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the TATA 407.
In this case, the Tribunal committed an error in fastening 10% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.
13. The accident occurred in the year 2015, the Tribunal considered Rs.9,000/- pm as income.
The accident occurred on 13.12.2015 though the claimants stated that the deceased was Mason, but they have not produced any documents.
Though the Tribunal considered Rs.9,000/- pm by taking the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority Chart, but the accident occurred at the end of 2015.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Service Authority Chart
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, it is proposed to take Rs.9,500/- pm as the income of the deceased.
If Rs.9,500/- pm is NC: 2024:KHC:27351 considered income, 25% would be added towards future prospects.
The Tribunal committed an error in deducting 50% towards personal and living expenses.

As there are three dependents i.e., a wife and two children, 1/3rd should be deducted towards personal and living Smt. Kanthamma vs Sri K L Manjunath on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164656946/
4 expenses.

entities.text: Smt. Kanthamma vs Sri K L Manjunath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the loss of dependency would be Rs.12,35,052/- (Rs.9,500 + 25% = Rs.11,875 - 1/3rd = Rs.7,917 x 12 x 13).
14. The Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards consortium.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others1,
appellant No.1 being the wife of the deceased, is entitled for loss of marital consortium of Rs.40,000/- and claimant Nos.2 and 3 being the sons of the deceased, are entitled for parental consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimants are entitled for a sum of (2018) 18 SCC 130 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:27351 Rs.1,20,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' as against Rs.40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

15. Towards 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses', Rs. 15,000/- each has been awarded by the Tribunal and Rs. 40,866/- is awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'medical expenses' and the same is kept intact.
16.
In view of the above, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,25,918/- as against Rs. 9,88,366/- as mentioned in the table below:

expenses 4 Medical expenses 40,866-00

Accordingly, I pass the following:
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:27351 ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed-in-part; II.

The judgment and award dated 05.02.2018 passed in MVC.No.1460/2016 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Bangalore (SCCH-17) is modified;
III.

The claimants are entitled for the compensation of Rs.14,25,918/- as against Rs.9,88,366/- awarded by the Tribunal;
IV.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal at the rate of 7.5% per annum on the compensation amount of Rs.9,88,366/- is left undisturbed.
